name: Aluminum (Generic)
generalDescription: Generic prototype for wrought aluminum alloys, suitable as a starter material for CAM exploration. Specific alloys (e.g. 6061-T6, 7075-T6, 2024-T3, cast alloys) can deviate significantly and are available in the Supplemental Materials addon. Surface speeds given for uncoated bits and conservative roughing conditions; coated bits and finishing setups can run substantially faster. Machinability values derived from Jonas Bähr's wrought-aluminum data (Tabellenbuch Zerspantechnik ISBN 978-3-7585-1315-2) released under CC-BY-3.0 in earlier FreeCAD releases.

name: Brass (Generic)
generalDescription: Generic prototype for general brass (Cu-Zn) alloys, suitable as a starter material for CAM exploration. Free-cutting brass (C36000) was historically the 100% machinability baseline and can run significantly faster than these defaults. Specific brass alloys are available in the Supplemental Materials addon. Surface speeds: derived from the brass HSS range of 90-210 m/min (Wikipedia "Speeds and feeds", CC-BY-SA-4.0); 120 m/min is mid-conservative. Unit cutting force and chip thickness exponent: published Kienzle-model reference values for the CuZn brass class.

name: Copper (Generic)
generalDescription: Generic prototype for unleaded annealed copper alloys, suitable as a starter material for CAM exploration. Pure copper is notoriously gummy; specific free-machining alloys (e.g. tellurium copper C145, sulfur copper C147) can run substantially faster. Specific copper alloys are available in the Supplemental Materials addon. Surface speeds: conservative values for uncoated bits roughing pure annealed copper, consistent with common engineering practice. Unit cutting force and chip thickness exponent: published Kienzle-model reference values for the copper class.

name: Plastic (Generic)
generalDescription: Generic prototype for engineering thermoplastics with POM/Delrin-class machinability, suitable as a starter material for CAM exploration. Soft plastics (HDPE, PE, PP) can run faster; reinforced or filled plastics (glass-filled nylon, carbon-filled PEEK) typically run slower with significantly higher tool wear. Specific plastic grades are available in the Supplemental Materials addon. Values are conservative engineering defaults for general-purpose thermoplastic machining.

name: Steel (Generic)
generalDescription: Generic prototype for soft unalloyed carbon steels (mild steel class), suitable as a starter material for CAM exploration. Specific grades (1018, 1045, 4140, A36, stainless variants, tool steels, etc.) deviate significantly and are available in the Supplemental Materials addon. Surface speeds given for uncoated bits and conservative roughing conditions; coated carbide bits can run 70%-260% faster. Machinability values derived from Jonas Bähr's mild-steel data (Tabellenbuch Zerspantechnik ISBN 978-3-7585-1315-2) released under CC-BY-3.0 in earlier FreeCAD releases.

name: Wood (Generic)
generalDescription: Generic prototype for hard woods around 0.75 g/cm^3 (beech, oak class), suitable as a starter material for CAM exploration. Wood is highly anisotropic and values are for the toughest crosscut direction (Kivimaa direction A). Specific wood species, softwoods, balsa, and engineered wood products (MDF, particleboard, plywood) are available in the Supplemental Materials addon. Surface speeds are conservative; capable machines with larger tools can run up to 4x faster. Cutting-force values use B.Ettelt's model adapted to FreeCAD's Machinability schema. Derived from Jonas Bähr's hard-wood data (Zerspanung von Holz und Holzwerkstoffen ISBN 978-3-446-47769-8) released under CC-BY-3.0 in earlier FreeCAD releases.
